transcript.text: I've just bought an AEG L7FEE865R and the Eco 40-60 wash says 3:39 and seems to take forever. My old machine did a 40 wash in an hour. Is it faulty? Should I send it back?

It is not faulty and you do not need to send it back. The 3 hours 39 minutes shown for the Eco 40-60 cycle is normal for this model; these programmes are designed to save energy by washing at lower temperatures for longer periods, which is why they take significantly longer than older machines or standard cotton cycles. The display time also adjusts dynamically as the machine weighs the laundry and balances the load. To be absolutely sure there isn't a heating issue (which would cause it to run even longer), you can check if the clothes are warm at the end of the cycle. If they come out warm, the heater is working correctly and the long time is just the programme doing its job.
I didn't notice if the clothes were warm at the end, sorry. When I touched the door during the wash it was only barely lukewarm, though. The clothes did come out clean. Is that normal for a 40 wash?

Yes, that is completely normal. The 'Eco 40-60' cycle is designed to clean effectively at lower temperatures by extending the wash time significantly—often up to four hours—to save electricity and water. Because it heats the water very gently over a long period, the door glass often only feels lukewarm even when the programme is working correctly. Since your clothes came out clean, the machine is performing exactly as intended.

candidates: Heating fault (machine stuck waiting for heat) (low)
